_comment: Figures that appear with their instrument in exactly one document, per DOCS-POLICY rule 2, and are cited rather than restated everywhere else. backend/tools/audit-docs.py check C4 reads this file and reports every match OUTSIDE the owner. A row is a name, the owning document, a regex, and an optional `allowed` list of fnmatch patterns where a copy is deliberate. Allowances are explicit rows, never a global ignore: 'we decided this copy is fine' is exactly the kind of decision that has to be written down where the next reader sees it. Matches inside fenced code blocks are skipped by the checker, so a shell transcript quoting a number is not a finding.
_why: The failure this prevents is already in the tree and is what motivated the rule. The main suite's test count is written as three different values in three live documents and none of them is what the runner prints; each was correct on the day it was typed. Nothing was wrong -- the number was copied to four places and only one of them was ever updated again. A general duplicate-number detector is not possible and must not be attempted, so this checks a DECLARED list. It will never be complete, and the declaration is as much the deliverable as the code is.
_scope_note: SEEDED WITH ONE ROW by task 36; the other seven added by task 38 (2026-08-01), which did the sweep. Task 36 deliberately invented no rows, because who owns what is the part of rule 2 a script cannot decide. Every row below states its owner, the measurement behind its pattern, and the reason for each allowance.
_allowance_rule: WHICH DOCUMENTS THIS CHECK BITES ON, and it is rule 1's lifecycle table rather than anyone's taste. `contract` and `rolling` may not be stale -- a stale contract is a defect and a rolling document is rewritten every session -- so those are where a copied figure is a real hazard and they are never allowed. `record`, `task` and `rationale` are FROZEN by construction: a record is history and says so, a task file freezes at its Status, and DOCS-POLICY's closing line is 'append-only means append-only'. Rewriting a figure in one of those destroys the only evidence the number was ever different, which is rule 4's whole argument and is what docs/archive/* was already allowed for. So the allowances below are frozen-kind documents, enumerated rather than globbed by kind because fnmatch cannot read frontmatter. They are enumerated to what each figure ACTUALLY REACHES today: a frozen document that starts quoting one of these later will fire once, and the fix is to add it here with a line saying why -- not to widen the rule.
_unit_note: THE UNIT OF A CLAIM IS THE SENTENCE, AND A STRUCK FIGURE IS NOT A RESTATEMENT. Both landed 2026-08-02 with task 46 and both are properties of the CHECKER, in `figure_hits()` -- stated once here rather than nine times below, which is this file's own rule applied to itself. (1) Every `^(?![^\n]*...)` lookahead below licenses a figure that names its metric or cites its owner, and it used to be scoped to the physical line. `.claude/CLAUDE.md` is hard-wrapped at ~88 columns, so a compliant sentence put `94.8%` on one line and the `agree2` licensing it on the next: the prose satisfied rule 3's corollary exactly as written and the check could not see it. Task 38's design was right against the corpus it was measured on -- docs/, where no registered figure straddled a wrap -- and widening the scanned set to the two roots is what moved the population. The licence is now tested against the SENTENCE, deliberately not the paragraph: measured 2026-08-02, the sentence licenses 3 lines and the paragraph 7, and the extra 4 are licensed by a token belonging to a DIFFERENT claim that happens to be adjacent. (2) A figure inside a `~~struck~~` span is exempt, per occurrence and not per sentence, so a live figure beside a struck one still fires. Rule 4 mandates struck-and-kept and 235 struck spans across 48 documents under docs/ are doing it; reporting a number whose own sentence disowns it penalises the one behaviour the policy requires outright. THE MATCH ITSELF IS STILL LINE-SCOPED and only the licence widened, which makes the new finding set a strict SUBSET of the old one by construction. Task 46 assumed that property held of the regexes -- 'widening a match can only ever CLEAR findings, never add them' -- and it does not: the webapp, labelling-rate and labelled-36 rows are proximity patterns, and a naive paragraph re-scope of the nine INVENTS 2 matches while clearing 10. Both invented matches are real cross-wrap occurrences in files these rows already allow, so the line scope has false negatives of the same shape as its false positives; widening the match body is a real follow-up with its own measurement, and it is not this change.
_owner_note: git show refactor-freeze-2026-08-02:docs/tasks/refactor/AUDIT.md owns the run-level figures because it was built for exactly that and its own header says it 'indexes; it does not restate'. It is NOT the owner of everything: the Pursuit gate volume is owned by git show refactor-freeze-2026-08-02:docs/pursuit-gate-volume.md, which carries the SQL, the date range and the junk-fraction adjustment. Rule 2 puts a figure with its instrument, and the instrument for that one is not in AUDIT.md.

figures.name: main suite test count
figures._note: OWNER MOVED 2026-08-18 (docs/adr/0010). It was git show refactor-freeze-2026-08-02:docs/tasks/refactor/AUDIT.md, deleted 2026-08-02, so the figure had no owner and every mention of it was a finding against a file that does not exist. Section 6 of STATE-OF-THE-SYSTEM.md is where figures now live with their instruments, so it owns this one. THE OWNER DOES NOT STATE THE NUMBER, and that is the intended end state rather than an omission: rule 3 says a number a script can produce is never typed into prose, so the suites table carries the command and the instruction to read `Ran N`. It did state it -- `Ran 1428` -- and the suite printed 1519 on 2026-08-18, which is the drift this row exists to catch and did not, because until 0010 widened scanned_files() the check could not see two of the three files that carry this figure.
figures._pattern_note: THE BAND WAS WIDENED FROM `11[0-9]{2}` AND THE OLD ONE WAS ALREADY BROKEN. The seeded pattern was written when the suite printed 1182; it printed 1233 the next day, which `11[0-9]{2}` cannot see at all -- the row silently stopped checking the live number within a day of being written, which is the same decay it exists to catch. `1[0-9]{3}` covers 1000-1999 and needs three exclusions, each measured on 2026-08-01 over every .md under docs/: (1) the seeded lookarounds refusing ':' '.' '-' and adjacent digits, which is what keeps `ingest/ats.py:1128` and `labels.py:1112-1145` out -- a naive \b11[0-9]{2}\b matched 86 lines of which 34 were LINE-NUMBER CITATIONS, and the lookarounds dropped all 34 and kept all 52; (2) '=' added to the lookbehind, which drops `$limit=1000` in git show refactor-freeze-2026-08-02:docs/ingest/nyc-open-data.md:83, the only false positive the widening introduced in a document this row bites on; (3) hex letters added to both lookarounds, which drops six matches inside sha256 digests and short commit hashes (`afb2d58f5d369dfd03ad9237a8b16396...`, `1074b7f0354bc3cceed49194`, `scratch_c1388ee2`). What remains is 69 lines over 7 files, of which exactly 3 are not test counts -- `1630` and `1285` in a source-volume table and `1099` as in the tax form -- and all 3 sit in frozen records that are allowed anyway. A check that cries wolf is worse than no check, because it teaches the reflex that retires all the others. RE-RECORDED 2026-08-02 BY TASK 46, against the sentence-scoped licence and the strikethrough exemption of `_unit_note`, over the CURRENT scanned set (docs/ plus the two roots). The 2026-08-01 counts above are superseded twice over -- they are line-scoped AND docs/-only -- and are kept because they are the measurement the pattern was SHAPED by, which the new counts do not replace. This row: 81 lines in 16 files line-scoped, 74 lines in 14 files now. All 7 cleared are STRUCK, none is a sentence effect, and every one is struck-and-kept history a reader is meant to see -- ~~1107~~, ~~1070~~, ~~1166~~, ~~1171~~ in git show refactor-freeze-2026-08-02:docs/archive/handoff-state-2026-07-31.md:31,56,95,96, a ~~1166~~ inside a strike spanning three lines in git show refactor-freeze-2026-08-02:docs/archive/handoff-tree-state.md:30-32, the `~~1182~~` this task's own file quotes at git show refactor-freeze-2026-08-02:docs/tasks/refactor/tranche_seven/46-sentence-scope-the-c4-lookahead.md:25, and `.claude/CLAUDE.md`'s struck suite figure. Six of the seven sit in files this row already allows, so the only one that was a FINDING is the last. THIS ROW IS THE REASON TASK 46 NEEDED A SECOND FIX: it is the one row of the nine with NO compliance lookahead, so no re-scoping of the licence could ever have cleared it -- joining the paragraph still matches `1182`. Task 46's premise that both C4 findings had one cause was wrong here, and only here.
figures._allowed_note: BOTH ALLOWANCES ARE NARROW AND NEITHER IS A SILENCED FINDING. TASKS.md carries a DATED baseline -- `1469` / `397` / `306`, re-measured 2026-08-09 -- whose whole purpose is stated in the sentence after it: the rows below quote older numbers and that is the point of the paragraph. A measurement carrying its date and its instrument is what rule 3 permits; a bare number in prose is what it forbids. DEV_TASKS.md is a FALSE POSITIVE and worth recording as one: the match at :592 is `1047` inside closed OQ-35, in the phrase 'line numbers as high as 1047' -- a line number in prose, not a test count. The pattern's lookarounds drop line-number CITATIONS of the form `<path>.py` followed by a colon and the number and cannot see this shape. Closed rows are frozen besides (OQ-33 owns whether a closed row's prose may be rewritten), so the fix would be to the pattern, not the file. If this figure ever needs to fire on DEV_TASKS.md, tighten the pattern first and drop this entry.

figures.name: webapp suite test count
figures._note: The webapp suite is the second half of the figure the first row is about, and it drifted in lockstep: every document that stated a stale main count stated this one beside it. Same treatment -- AUDIT.md carries the command, not the number.
figures._value_note: THIS ROW PINNED THE LITERAL `93` AND THEREFORE PROTECTED A NUMBER THAT NO LONGER EXISTS -- found and fixed 2026-08-02. The webapp suite has not printed 93 since well before this row was written; it printed 344 on the day this was found. So the row could match only a STALE copy of a superseded value, and every one of those sits in a frozen document this row already allows: measured, the old pattern was 7 matches in 4 files and 0 FINDINGS, and no possible live restatement could ever have made it fire. A row that cannot fire is worse than no row, because it appears in the declared list and reads as coverage. THE MAIN-SUITE ROW ABOVE ALREADY LEARNED THIS and its `_pattern_note` says so in capitals -- it was seeded as `11[0-9]{2}` while the suite printed 1182, the suite printed 1233 the next day, and the row silently stopped checking the live number within a day of being written. That row was widened to a band. This one was left pinned, so the same decay ran for longer and quieter. Rule 3's principle is the diagnosis: a figure a script can produce must never be typed into prose, and a CHECK that hard-codes the figure's current VALUE is the same mistake one level down -- it is a typed number pretending to be an instrument. THE FIX IS TO KEY ON THE COUNT'S FORM, NEVER ITS VALUE, so the row survives every future run of the suite. Note what is NOT wrong here: the owner is right and AUDIT.md deliberately types no count at all, exactly as the main-suite row's `_note` prescribes. An owner with no copy is the intended end state; the defect was entirely in the pattern.
figures._pattern_note: TWO ARMS, BOTH VALUE-INDEPENDENT, MEASURED 2026-08-02 BEFORE BEING WRITTEN. Arm 1 is the runner's own output -- `webapp` within 60 characters of `Ran <n> tests` -- which is the exact string AUDIT.md and .claude/CLAUDE.md both instruct readers to quote instead of a static count, so keying on it rewards the compliant form and catches any value. Arm 2 is the digest idiom the run log uses, `Suite **1166 -> 1171**, webapp **93**`, anchored on the word `suite` before `webapp` and requiring the bold markers. Together: 8 lines in 4 files, 0 FINDINGS, and every one of the 8 is a genuine restatement of this figure at four different values (55, 75, 93, 147, 159). ZERO FALSE POSITIVES, which is the bar this file sets and which the obvious alternatives all fail. Three were measured and REJECTED rather than assumed. (a) A digit BAND like the main-suite row's: `\d{2,4}` near `webapp` gives 6 findings and not one is the figure -- `test_event_replay.py: 20`, `/v1/auth/login` returns **503**, port **8420**, and `backend/webapp/.env` verified **2026**. The main row's band works because a 4-digit count has a distinctive shape and `webapp` does not; this row's proximity token co-occurs with ports, paths, dates and HTTP statuses, so a band here is exactly the check that cries wolf. (b) Narrowing that band to `9[0-9]|[1-9][0-9]{2}` still keeps the **503**, in HANDOFF.md -- the one `kind: rolling` document, the worst possible place to raise a false finding. (c) Arm 2 WITHOUT the `suite` anchor keeps the **503** too; the anchor is what separates a test-count digest from a status code, and it is a real token in the idiom rather than a word added to quiet a finding. THE OLD 2026-08-01 AND TASK 46 COUNTS FOR THIS ROW ARE SUPERSEDED AND ARE KEPT BELOW, because they are the measurement the OLD pattern was shaped by and they document how long a pinned value went unnoticed. Note that arm 1 makes the task 47 false negative WORSE, not better, and this is recorded rather than hidden: `git show refactor-freeze-2026-08-02:docs/tasks/refactor/tranche_five/git show refactor-freeze-2026-08-02:docs/tasks/refactor/tranche_five/29-labelling-session.md:791-792` puts `backend/webapp/` on one line and `Ran 93 tests` on the next, so the line-scoped match still cannot see it. That is task 47's to fix and it is not made harder by this change. SUPERSEDED, and kept: A BARE `93` IS UNUSABLE AND THIS IS THE ROW THAT PROVES THE POINT. Measured 2026-08-01 over docs/: `(?<![\d.:\-])93(?![\d.%])` matches 68 lines in 14 files, and almost none of them are this figure -- `93 s` (the labelling rate, a different row below), `[93-100]` in a confidence interval, `93.3%` per-platform agreement, `f5a93a4` and `1d665f5`-style commit hashes, `workflow automation | 93` in a vocabulary count. Requiring the word `webapp` on the same line and within 60 characters before the number takes it to 6 lines in 3 files, every one of them the suite count. The `\s*s\b` exclusion is there so a future line reading 'webapp ... 93 s' cannot be caught by the wrong row. The line-start negative lookahead means a document that cites AUDIT.md on the same line is compliant with rule 2 and is not a finding, which is what rule 2 asks for rather than a blanket ban on the digits. RE-RECORDED 2026-08-02 BY TASK 46, against the sentence-scoped licence and the strikethrough exemption of `_unit_note`, over the CURRENT scanned set (docs/ plus the two roots). The 2026-08-01 counts above are superseded twice over -- they are line-scoped AND docs/-only -- and are kept because they are the measurement the pattern was SHAPED by, which the new counts do not replace. This row: 5 lines in 2 files, line-scoped and now, unchanged. The proximity construction is why it is also the row that proves widening the MATCH would not be free: a naive paragraph re-scope invents a match at git show refactor-freeze-2026-08-02:docs/tasks/refactor/tranche_five/git show refactor-freeze-2026-08-02:docs/tasks/refactor/tranche_five/29-labelling-session.md:792, where `backend/webapp/` ends one line and `Ran 93 tests` opens the next. That one is a REAL occurrence the line scope cannot see, in a file this row allows.
figures._allowed_note: Frozen kinds; see _allowance_rule. HANDOFF.md is again not allowed, for the reason in the row above.

figures._note: 94.8% is `agree2` -- repeat 1 against repeat 2, n=115, deepseek-v4-flash at temperature 0. It is the most-quoted number in this run and it circulated for four days with `--repeat 3` beside it, which names the RUN and not the metric. AUDIT.md section 'The three self-consistency metrics' owns all three with the command that reproduces them from docs/ingestion_tests/selfcheck-n120-2026-07-28.json -- committed data, no LLM call, no cost to re-derive.
figures._pattern_note: THIS ROW ENFORCES rule 3's corollary, not a ban on the digits: 'cite the metric, not just the value'. The line-start negative lookahead makes any line that names `agree2`, `pairwise` or `unanimous`, or cites AUDIT.md, compliant -- which is exactly the form the fix takes. Measured 2026-08-01: the bare number matches 14 lines in 6 files; with the lookahead, 9 lines in 4 files. The 5 it drops all already name their metric or their owner, so a row without it would have reported five documents for doing the right thing. group(0) runs from the start of the line, so the CLI prints the sentence rather than the digits, which is more useful anyway. RE-RECORDED 2026-08-02 BY TASK 46, against the sentence-scoped licence and the strikethrough exemption of `_unit_note`, over the CURRENT scanned set (docs/ plus the two roots). The 2026-08-01 counts above are superseded twice over -- they are line-scoped AND docs/-only -- and are kept because they are the measurement the pattern was SHAPED by, which the new counts do not replace. This row: 9 lines in 5 files line-scoped, 8 lines in 4 files now. The single line cleared is `.claude/CLAUDE.md:127`, whose sentence ends `n=115, both **`agree2`** (task 06)` on the next physical line -- the defect task 46 was opened for, and the compliant form this row's lookahead was written to reward.
figures._allowed_note: docs/ingestion_tests/* is the one place where rule 2's 'exactly one document' is genuinely arguable, and it is allowed rather than argued away. That directory HOLDS THE INSTRUMENT -- selfcheck-n120-2026-07-28.json is the file the command reads -- and its README carries the per-field table for all sixteen fields with the metric named in the COLUMN HEADER, which is the compliant form for a table and is what a per-cell rule cannot see. AUDIT.md links to it as the deeper document. The other two are frozen kinds per _allowance_rule; git show refactor-freeze-2026-08-02:docs/tasks/refactor/tranche_five/29-labelling-session.md's use already ends 'cross-referenced from docs/ingestion_tests/README.md rather than restated here', which is rule 2 being followed by hand before there was a check.
